patch_resolves_note: On the staged original PoC, the fixed build still reaches `mpz_get_int` with `digits(y)=1` but no longer executes the second-limb probe guarded by `d == 2`. A nearby two-limb bigint witness exercises that protected event in the fixed build with `digits(y)=2`, confirming the missing vulnerable obligation rather than a vacuous clean exit.

root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `mpz_get_int` reads `y->p[1]`, the bigint must have exactly two live limbs, so the second-limb probe executes only when `digits(y) == 2`.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable guard falls through from `digits(y) == 1` into `y->p[1] > 1`. The fixed code adds the missing `d == 2` gate before any second-limb read.

nodes.state: The sink-side second-limb probe reads exactly the same address as the root guard's computed `y->p + 1`, i.e. the one-past element of the single-limb allocation.
When `mpz_pow(..., 0)` materializes value `1`, `mpz_set_int` requests one limb and `mpz_realloc` leaves the bigint extent at exactly one limb.

edges.relation: The one-limb extent allocated for value `1` is the same bigint extent later presented to `mpz_get_int` at the missing guard.
The missing root-side guard leaves the exact computed second-limb address live into the sink read of `y->p[1]`.
